svg.aria-label: Same question, plain Claude versus /think. Plain Claude returns a four-step checklist and asks for more information. /think returns one call (freeze it, finish only if another customer commits), catches that the only demand evidence came from the customer who churned, and gives a next step and a kill criterion.
svg.text: claude
claude + /think
$ claude "We spent 6 months building a feature our
biggest customer asked for, and they just churned.
It's 80% done. Should we finish it?"
Ignore the 6 months. The only question that matters:
would you spend the remaining effort to ship it?
## 1. Get an honest estimate of the remaining 20%
## 2. Check whether anyone else wants it
## 3. Find out why they churned
## 4. Look for options between finishing and
abandoning
## My default
Pause unless you can name 3+ other customers who want
it.
If you share how many other customers have asked for
this ... I can help you make the call.
~440 words · a checklist · ends by asking you for more
$ claude "/think We spent 6 months building a feature
our biggest customer asked for, and they just
churned. It's 80% done. Should we finish it?"
Call: Freeze it. Finish only if another customer
commits.
Sampling: all the demand evidence came from one
customer, and they just left. That counts against
it.
Sunk cost: starting today, would you build it? With
the requester gone, probably not.
Opportunity cost: those weeks could go to whatever
lost you your biggest customer.
Mom Test: don't ask "would you use X?", ask what their
workaround costs today.
Next: interview your top 5–8 accounts this week, and
ask the churned customer why they left.
Change course if: 2+ customers commit (pilot, contract
term, renewal).
~360 words · one call · a kill criterion
